notes:
## Shakshouka
Shakshouka is a Maghrebi dish of eggs poached in a sauce of tomatoes, olive oil, peppers, onion, and garlic, commonly spiced with cumin, paprika, and cayenne pepper. Shakshouka is a popular dish throughout North Africa and the Middle East.

## The Shakshuka System
The Shakshuka System (Hebrew: שיטת השקשוקה) is a 2008 Israeli documentary film created by the Israeli investigative journalist Mickey Rosenthal and the Israeli director Ilan Aboody. The film focuses on the connection between private capital and government in Israel and suggests that a system exists whereby the State of Israel sells its limited resources, cheaply, to a handful of wealthy families. The film shows this by specifically focusing on the business relationship between the political leadership in Israel and one of the wealthiest families in the Israeli economy – the Ofer family.
The film won the Ophir Award for Best Documentary film in 2009.
While the film was being produced, the Ofer Brothers Group filed a lawsuit against the creators of the film and no Israeli TV channel would show it. Initially the film was screened in Cinematheques, different events, and in the Knesset. A year after the premiere, it was broadcast on Channel 1, followed by a film produced by the Ofer Brothers in response. In February 2010 the lawsuit was dismissed.

## Pilpelchuma
Pilpelchuma (Hebrew: פלפלצ'ומה), also spelled pilpelshuma (lit: "pepper garlic"), is a chilli-garlic paste similar to a hot sauce originating from the Libyan Jews and commonly used in Israeli cuisine.

plan.title: Shakshuka: Eggs Poached in Spiced Tomato Sauce
plan.description: Shakshuka is a Maghrebi dish of eggs poached in a sauce of tomatoes, olive oil, peppers, onion, and garlic. Learn what goes into it, how it comes together, and how to serve it.

beats.narration: Imagine a single pan holding a bubbling red sauce, with eggs gently cooking right in the middle. That is shakshuka, a dish that turns simple ingredients into a feast.

props.alt: Shakshuka with eggs in tomato sauce

beats.narration: Shakshuka is a Maghrebi dish, meaning it comes from North Africa's west. Eggs are poached in a sauce of tomatoes, olive oil, peppers, onion, and garlic.

props.definition: A Maghrebi dish of eggs poached in a sauce of tomatoes, olive oil, peppers, onion, and garlic.

beats.narration: Today it is popular throughout North Africa and the Middle East. You will find it on breakfast tables, at brunch spots, and in family kitchens from morning until night.

props.title: Where shakshuka is loved
props.caption: North Africa and the Middle East

beats.narration: Let's look at what goes in. You need tomatoes, olive oil, peppers, onion, garlic, and of course eggs. Nothing fancy, and most of it is probably in your kitchen.
The flavor comes from the spices. Cumin adds earthiness, paprika adds color and sweetness, and cayenne pepper brings the heat. Adjust them to your own taste.
Many cooks add a spoonful of pilpelchuma on the side. It is a chilli and garlic paste from Libyan Jews, used widely in Israeli cuisine, and the name means pepper garlic.

props.definition: A chilli-garlic paste, similar to a hot sauce, originating from the Libyan Jews and commonly used in Israeli cuisine.

beats.narration: Now the method. First, heat olive oil and soften the onion and peppers. Then add garlic and spices. Next, pour in the tomatoes and let the sauce simmer. Finally, crack in the eggs.
Cover the pan and let the eggs poach gently in the sauce. Watch closely. You want the whites set and the yolks still soft, ready to be broken into the sauce.

props.alt: Simmering pan of sauce on stove

beats.narration: Bring the pan straight to the table. Scoop it up with warm bread, so every bite catches a bit of sauce, a bit of egg, and a little heat.
So that is shakshuka: eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce, built from humble ingredients. Make it once, and you will understand why so many kitchens share it.

props.text: Simple ingredients, one pan, a dish shared across continents.
